AppShellDensity.name: AppShellDensity
AppShellDensity.description: The type step an app sets once on its `AppShell`: `compact` is one step down for the whole app.

AvatarShape.name: AvatarShape
AvatarShape.description: `round` for a person, `square` (rounded corners that grow with the size) for an org or a team.

AvatarStackPerson.name: AvatarStackPerson
AvatarStackPerson.description: One member of an `AvatarStack`: the same `name` and optional local `src` an `Avatar` takes.

BarTone.name: BarTone
BarTone.description: The colour of a bar's fill.

BottomSheetSnap.name: BottomSheetSnap
BottomSheetSnap.description: A snap height: a number from 0 to 1 is a share of the parent's height, a `"120px"` string is pixels.

ButtonSize.name: ButtonSize
ButtonSize.description: A Button's height and text, on the library's one `Size` scale.

ButtonTone.name: ButtonTone
ButtonTone.description: A Button's tones: `neutral` (the accent fill, the default), `positive` and `danger`.

ButtonVariant.name: ButtonVariant
ButtonVariant.description: A Button's look: `primary` the one main action, `outline` and `ghost` the others, `link` text in running text, `dashed` the add-another row.

CellTone.name: CellTone
CellTone.description:
The text of a cell: its weight and colour. `neutral` (the default), `strong` and `muted` are the
plain ones; the rest are the shared tones, for an amount that carries a meaning (a gain, an
overspend). Colour alone does not say it, so a signed figure or a word says it too.

ClusterAlign.name: ClusterAlign
ClusterAlign.description: Where a `Cluster`'s items sit across the row: `center`, `baseline` for mixed text sizes, `start` or `end`.

ClusterGap.name: ClusterGap
ClusterGap.description: The first three steps of `Stack`'s scale: `xs` between items in a line, `sm` inside a group, `md` between blocks.

ClusterGrowMinWidth.name: ClusterGrowMinWidth
ClusterGrowMinWidth.description: The narrowest a `ClusterGrow` gets before the row wraps: `sm` or `md`.

ClusterJustify.name: ClusterJustify
ClusterJustify.description: Where a `Cluster`'s items sit along the row: `start`, `end`, or `between` to spread them to both ends.

CodeLanguage.name: CodeLanguage
CodeLanguage.description: The languages a `CodeBlock` colours; `text` is plain, and `console` marks the commands of a terminal session.

ColourScheme.name: ColourScheme
ColourScheme.description: The two colour schemes a site switches between: `light` and `dark`.

ColourSchemeClasses.name: ColourSchemeClasses
ColourSchemeClasses.description: The class each scheme puts on `<html>`: none for light and `dark` for dark, unless the app's theme says otherwise (a light theme with a scope class of its own).

ControlSize.name: ControlSize
ControlSize.description: A control's size: the library's one `Size` scale.

ControlWidth.name: ControlWidth
ControlWidth.description: `full` fills the parent (the default); `fill` grows to the space left in a flex row; `auto` adds no width class, so the control is as wide as the browser makes it; the rest are fixed.

Crumb.name: Crumb
Crumb.description:
A crumb that links: `href`, drawn by the app's router link through `LinkProvider` for an in-app
path, else a plain `<a>`. `external` opens in a new tab. The last crumb is the current page and is
never a link.
Crumb.definition: { label: ReactNode; href: string; external?: boolean }

DateRange.name: DateRange
DateRange.description: A from and to date: `start` on or before `end`.

DateRangePreset.name: DateRangePreset
DateRangePreset.description: A ready-made range the app builds from its own today, such as "Last 7 days".

DocsHeading.name: DocsHeading
DocsHeading.description: One entry of "On this page": a heading's id, its text and its level.

DocsNavGroup.name: DocsNavGroup
DocsNavGroup.description: One group of the docs nav: a title over its links (`Tab`s with an `href`). A group with no title is the nav's top.

DocsNeighbour.name: DocsNeighbour
DocsNeighbour.description: The page before or after this one in reading order.

FormRowSpan.name: FormRowSpan
FormRowSpan.description: Relative widths in a `FormRow`: a field of `span` 2 is twice as wide as one of `span` 1.

IconButtonVariant.name: IconButtonVariant
IconButtonVariant.description: An IconButton's look: `outline` with a border, or `ghost` with none until hover.

IconName.name: IconName
IconName.description: The names of the icon set: feature ideas, then UI glyphs, then the ideas the docs sections stand for.

ImageAspect.name: ImageAspect
ImageAspect.description:
The shapes an image is cropped or letterboxed to, or `natural`: no shape of its own, so the
picture keeps its own proportions.

ImageWidth.name: ImageWidth
ImageWidth.description: How wide an image is: `full` fills its parent; the others are 96, 160 or 256px, capped at the parent's width.

LegendItem.name: LegendItem
LegendItem.description: One entry of a `Legend`: the `label` the colour stands for, its swatch, and an optional `detail` (a count, a share) after it.
LegendItem.definition: { label: string; tone: VizTone; swatch?: "solid" | "dashed"; detail?: string | number }

LinkAdapter.name: LinkAdapter
LinkAdapter.description: Draws one in-app link: the app's router `<Link>`, handed `LinkAdapterProps`.

LinkAdapterProps.name: LinkAdapterProps
LinkAdapterProps.description:
What the app's `LinkAdapter` receives to draw an in-app link with its router's `<Link>`: the
destination as `href` (search and hash included), the component's classes, its label as
`children`, and (for a tab that is current, or an option with a tooltip) `aria-current`, `target`,
`rel` and `title`. `@hackcove/ui-react` has no router dependency.

An optional field is `?: T`, never `?: T | undefined`, and a key that has no value is left out
rather than set to `undefined`. A router's `<Link>` declares its props that way, so under
`exactOptionalPropertyTypes` the spread compiles. Any other anchor prop the caller gave the
component (`id`, `data-*`, `download`, a handler) arrives too, untyped here, and `<Link>`
takes it as its own.
LinkAdapterProps.definition: { href: string; className: string; children: ReactNode; aria-current?: AriaCurrent; target?: string; rel?: string; title?: string }

MenuAction.name: MenuAction
MenuAction.description: One entry of a `Menu`: an action that runs `onSelect`, or a link to `href`. Never both.
MenuAction.definition: { label: string; icon?: IconName | undefined; tone?: IconButtonTone | undefined; disabled?: boolean | undefined; } & ({ onSelect: () => void; href?: undefined; external?: undefined; } | { onSelect?: undefined; href: string; external?: boolean | undefined; })

MetaListSeparator.name: MetaListSeparator
MetaListSeparator.description: The mark between MetaList items: `·`, `•`, or `none` for a gap alone.

PillTone.name: PillTone
PillTone.description: A Pill's tones: the five meanings, and `accent` for a category that is none of them.

RegionRect.name: RegionRect
RegionRect.description: A box in a picture's own units (an image's pixels): its top-left corner and its size.
RegionRect.definition: { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number }

RowTone.name: RowTone
RowTone.description:
The status of a row: the Callout's tones, plus `muted`. A toned row gets a stripe on its leading
edge and the tone's soft fill; `muted` fades the row instead, for one that matters less. The
stripe takes the tone's text colour, which every theme already remaps, so no new palette entry.

SectionSize.name: SectionSize
SectionSize.description: A `Section`'s scale: `sm` a small titled group, `md` a page's section, `lg` a landing page's section.

Segment.name: Segment
Segment.description: One option of a SegmentedControl. See `SwitchItem`.

SideColumnWidth.name: SideColumnWidth
SideColumnWidth.description: How wide a `SideColumn`'s aside is from `lg`: `sm` 18rem, `md` 24rem, or `third` a third of the row.

SiteFooterLink.name: SiteFooterLink
SiteFooterLink.description: One link in a `SiteFooter`'s row: its words, where it goes, and whether it opens a new tab.
SiteFooterLink.definition: { label: string; href: string; external?: boolean }

SiteSearchItem.name: SiteSearchItem
SiteSearchItem.description: One page the search can find.
SiteSearchItem.definition: { label: string; description?: string; href: string; keywords?: string[] }

Size.name: Size
Size.description:
The one size scale of the library: `sm`, `md` and `lg`, with `md` the default. This is the one
list of where it goes further and where the default is not `md`; the README and the docs point
here rather than count them again.

Past `sm`, `md` and `lg`, only where there is a real use, and no scale skips `md`:
- `Avatar` and `AvatarStack` `size`: also `xs`, `xl`, `2xl` and `3xl`.
- The gap scale (`Stack`, `Section` and `ProseLayout` `gap`): also `xs` and `xl`.
- `Cluster` and `ScrollStrip` `gap`: `xs`, `sm` and `md`, the first steps of the gap scale.
- `Icon` `size`: also `feature`, the mark of a feature card.
- `Dialog` `width`: also `full`, the whole screen. `ChatThread` `height`: also `fill`, its parent's.

Defaults that are not `md`:
- `Table` `size` is `sm`, its row padding, and the buttons and pills in a table take that size;
  a field keeps `md`.
- `Cluster` and `ScrollStrip` `gap` are `sm`: the items of a row sit closer than the blocks of a
  column.
- `Stack` and `Section` `gap` are `xs` inside a `Card`, `Dialog`, `Drawer`, `BottomSheet`,
  `Callout` or `ListRow`.
- A `Pill`, `Button` or `IconButton` with no `size` takes the size of the `Card`, `ListRow` or
  `Table` it sits in; an `EmptyState` takes its slot's.

With no `size` at all, because they take the size of the text or the control they sit on:
`Callout`, `CopyButton`, `Kbd`, `Badge` and `Breadcrumbs`.

SortableMove.name: SortableMove
SortableMove.description: A move the user made: which item, the section it lands in, and the item it lands next to.
SortableMove.definition: { id: string; section?: string; target?: { id: string; position: "before" | "after" } }

StackAlign.name: StackAlign
StackAlign.description: Where a Stack's children sit across the column: `stretch` spans it, `start` keeps each child's own width.

StackedSegment.name: StackedSegment
StackedSegment.description: One part of a `StackedBar`: its `label`, its `value` (its share is `value` over the sum) and its colour.
StackedSegment.definition: { label: string; value: number; tone: VizTone }

StackGap.name: StackGap
StackGap.description: The space between a `Stack`'s blocks, on the gap scale: `xs` 8px, `sm` 16px, `md` 24px, `lg` 32px, `xl` 48px (64px from `sm`).

StackRowFrom.name: StackRowFrom
StackRowFrom.description: The breakpoint from which a `Stack` turns from a column into a row: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

StackWidth.name: StackWidth
StackWidth.description: A `Stack`'s width cap at the start edge: `compact`, `narrow` (a reading measure), `default`, `wide` or `full`.

StatTileTone.name: StatTileTone
StatTileTone.description: The colour of a tile's value (and of its accent bar): plain ink, green, amber or red.

StepsSize.name: StepsSize
StepsSize.description: A `Steps` scale: `md` the small list down a column, `lg` the steps across a landing page.

SubsectionHeadingSize.name: SubsectionHeadingSize
SubsectionHeadingSize.description: A SubsectionHeading's type size: `sm` a form-group caption, `md` a card title, `lg` a drawer title.

Tab.name: Tab
Tab.description: One tab of a Tabs row. See `SwitchItem`.

TableSort.name: TableSort
TableSort.description: Where a sortable column stands: ARIA's own words. `none` is a column the table is not sorted by.

TextAlign.name: TextAlign
TextAlign.description: Where a run of text sits across its block.

TextLines.name: TextLines
TextLines.description: How many lines a clamped run shows before it ends in an ellipsis.

TextLinkSize.name: TextLinkSize
TextLinkSize.description: A TextLink's pinned type size, on the `Size` scale; left out, it takes the size of the text around it.

TextMinWidth.name: TextMinWidth
TextMinWidth.description: A fixed width for a run of text: `amount` is a money figure, right-aligned, at a width that lines a column up.

TextTone.name: TextTone
TextTone.description:
The meaning of a run of inline text: the library's `Tone`, plus `muted` for a quieter line and
`accent` for the theme's accent ink. `neutral` (the default) is the role's own ink. Colour alone
does not say a meaning, so the words do too.

Toast.name: Toast
Toast.description: One notice in a `ToastRegion`. The caller holds the list; the region draws it.
Toast.definition: { id: string; title: string; body?: ReactNode; tone?: Tone; actions?: ReactNode }

Tone.name: Tone
Tone.description:
The one tone vocabulary of the library: what a thing means, not what colour it is. `neutral`
(no meaning, the role's own ink or surface) is every component's default, `info` is a note,
`positive` a success, `warn` a caution and `danger` an error or a destructive act.

A component extends it outward only where it has a real use, and says so beside its own type:
the text roles add `muted` (a quieter line) and `accent` (the theme's accent ink), `Pill` and the
charts add `accent` for a category that is none of the five meanings. No component renames a
tone (`negative`, `default`, `slate` and the colour names are gone), and no scale skips `neutral`.

TrendSeries.name: TrendSeries
TrendSeries.description:
One series of a `TrendChart`: its `label` (the table's column, the Legend's entry), its colour,
and one value per bucket in the buckets' order. A `null`, or a list shorter than the buckets, is
a missing value.
TrendSeries.definition: { label: string; tone: VizTone; values: readonly (number | null)[] }

VizTone.name: VizTone
VizTone.description:
The colour of a `StackedBar` segment, a `Legend` swatch or a `TrendChart` series: the `TextTone`
names, painted as a fill, or a category colour, `cat1` to `cat8`. On a chart `neutral` is a grey
of its own that sits apart from `muted` (for "unmeasured" next to "same"), and `accent` is the
theme's accent, apart from `info`. Categories with no meaning take `cat1` upwards in order; good
and bad take the meaning tones; one chart never mixes the two.
